security_audit.summary: Five findings are confirmed because the skill directs users or agents to run external CLI commands, invoke remote applications, or install unpinned skills. The remaining findings are Markdown syntax, ordinary links, marketing text, or event-planning guidance with no shell execution or reconnaissance behavior.

remediation.issue: The installation commands reference mutable, unpinned skill sources.
remediation.suggestion: Pin each dependency to a reviewed commit or release, publish integrity information, and require confirmation before installation.

remediation.issue: The belt examples invoke remote applications and may transmit prompts or selected files to third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the destination services, require confirmation before each call, and warn users not to submit confidential content.

content.user_title: Plan a Strong Product Hunt Launch
content.value_statement: Product Hunt launches require coordinated listing content, visuals, timing, and engagement. This skill provides specifications, templates, research commands, and a launch-day playbook.
actual_capabilities: Applies documented limits for taglines, descriptions, gallery images, and topics.
Plans a five-image gallery sequence around product value, features, transformation, proof, and differentiation.
Generates tagline options from clear formulas and evaluates common wording problems.
Structures a maker comment around the product, founder story, differentiator, roadmap, and feedback request.
Builds preparation, launch-day, engagement, and post-launch checklists.
Provides belt CLI examples for image generation and competitive research.
limitations: Image generation and web research require the external belt CLI, authentication, and third-party services.
The skill does not publish a Product Hunt listing or monitor launch results automatically.
Platform specifications and recommended timing can change after the skill is published.
Generated images and copy require review for accuracy, brand fit, permissions, and current Product Hunt rules.

use_cases.title: Prepare a startup launch
use_cases.description: Create listing copy, a gallery sequence, a maker comment, and a launch-day schedule for a new software product.

use_cases.title: Launch a side project
use_cases.description: Turn a brief product description into focused taglines, visual priorities, and a manageable engagement checklist.

use_cases.title: Coordinate campaign assets
use_cases.description: Align copy, image requirements, research, community outreach, and follow-up tasks across a launch team.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a basic listing
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft my Product Hunt listing for [product], which helps [audience] achieve [benefit]. Provide five taglines under 60 characters and a concise description.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the product positioning is clear but the listing copy is not written.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the gallery
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a five-image gallery plan for [product]. For each image, state the message, visual content, and proof needed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when designers need an ordered asset brief.

prompt_templates.title: Write the maker comment
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a maker comment for [product] using this founder story: [story]. Include the problem, differentiator, next step, and a feedback question.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the launch needs a personal opening comment.

prompt_templates.title: Build the full launch plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a complete launch plan for [product] targeting [audience] on [date]. Include preparation, timing, outreach, engagement checkpoints, and post-launch follow-up. Flag assumptions and policy risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when coordinating a complete campaign with several contributors.

output_examples.input: Create taglines for a tool that turns SQL queries into dashboards for data teams.
output: Turn SQL into dashboards in seconds
Visualize every query without BI setup

output_examples.input: Plan the first three gallery images for a scheduling assistant.
output: Hero: Show the assistant arranging a real calendar and state the time saved.
Feature: Demonstrate a meeting request becoming an available time slot.
Transformation: Compare manual calendar coordination with the completed automated schedule.

output_examples.input: Outline a maker comment for a customer feedback product.
output_examples.output: Open with the product result. Explain the customer research problem, describe the differentiator, share the next milestone, and ask for specific feedback.

best_practices: Verify current Product Hunt specifications and policies before finalizing the listing.
Use real product screens, accurate claims, and evidence that reviewers can inspect.
Review every external command and remove confidential information before using third-party services.
anti_patterns: Do not ask users for upvotes or use spam-like community outreach.
Do not publish vague taglines, unsupported metrics, or generic gallery images.
Do not install unpinned dependencies or send private assets to external tools without review.

faq.question: Does this skill publish my Product Hunt listing?
faq.answer: No. It prepares copy, visuals, research, and schedules, but you must submit and manage the listing.

faq.question: Do I need the belt CLI?
faq.answer: Only the image-generation and web-research examples require belt. The planning guidance and writing templates work without it.

faq.question: Can it create gallery images?
faq.answer: It provides belt commands and prompts for external image services. Review generated assets for accuracy, dimensions, permissions, and brand consistency.

faq.question: Are the Product Hunt limits always current?
faq.answer: No. Product Hunt can change specifications and policies, so verify them before launch.

faq.question: Does the skill guarantee launch ranking?
faq.answer: No. Ranking depends on product quality, audience response, competition, platform decisions, and other factors outside the skill.

faq.question: How should I handle external research and image tools?
faq.answer: Review each command, confirm the service destination, and exclude confidential prompts, files, credentials, and customer data.
